<!-- impact:shell-launch:Config1 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Windows Shell Spoofing Vulnerability | [KB5099414](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202) | CVE-2026-32202 | Low Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: Config1
- Model / role: CTConsole-A300 / ct-imaging-workstation
- Deployment group: imaging-ct
- OS: Windows 11 IoT Enterprise build 10.0.22621.2500
- Clinical criticality: high
- Network exposure: restricted_lan

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | C | C | C |
| Product | M | M | M |

Letters are C / H / M / L. Vendor comes from FindUpdates severity, KEV, and exploitability. Product is allowed to be lower when the patched component is not loaded.

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

- `src/HostApplication/HostApplication.csproj` — `UseWPF`, WinExe, `net9.0-windows`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `dotnet publish` `--self-contained true` `-r win-x64`.
- `src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs` — `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt`.
- `src/HostApplication.Core/SystemInformation.cs` — `RuntimeInformation` host strings.
- `src/HostApplication/app.manifest` — Windows 10 compatibility and `PerMonitorV2`.
- `src/HostApplication.Core/InsecureVendorBulletinClient.cs` — HTTPS via host Schannel.
- SBOM present at `workspace/sbom/HostApplication.sbom.spdx.json`.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** The published WinExe still exists without this KB. Shell identity is a host path, not a product library load.
- **If we install: App may break.** A host Shell KB can change how `OutputType=WinExe` and `app.manifest` assembly identity launch.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Leaving the KB off leaves host Shell unpatched. The app file is unchanged.
- **Compatibility: Unknown.** We did not prove launch will fail on current `main`; there is no UI/launch automation test.

### Conclusions

Shell may change exe launch or identity. Current `main` has no third-party PackageReference. CI publishes a self-contained win-x64 exe, so an OS .NET KB does not patch the bundled runtime.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-32202 in KB5099414. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed that the WinExe launch path has such host Shell dependency.

## Product Risk assessment

- Affected product functions: process launch and exe identity.
- Potential hazards: operator cannot start the client if Shell identity handling changes.
- Failure scenarios: install — launch may fail; skip — host Shell stays exposed.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers this coupling.

### Gap Analysis

- No Unit, Smoke, or Regression case in `docs/test-plan.md` for this host path.
- No UI automation.

## Recommendation

Low Prio: do not treat this host KB as a product patch for Config1 (`shell-launch`). Keep it off the product install set.
